articles.title: Joe Milton Joins Cowboys Practice Squad After QB Goes Unclaimed on Waivers
articles.summary: Although the Dallas Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, he is remaining with the organization after signing with the practice squad.
articles.body:
Although the Dallas Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, he is remaining with the organization after signing with the practice squad.

Both COO/co-owner Stephen Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer had expressed significant interest in having the signal-caller back in the mix via the practice squad after his release earlier in the week.

Jones made his remarks on the DLLS Cowboys podcast, and Schottenheimer revealed his feelings to reporters during his Tuesday press conference.

The Cowboys were fortunate to get that chance to bring him back after Milton went unclaimed on waivers.

Milton initially made the 53-man roster after cuts were announced on Sunday. However, Dallas changed course after claiming running back Emari Demercado off waivers from the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday.

The Cowboys started with three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster in starter Dak Prescott, Milton and Sam Howell, although it was unclear who the Cowboys would choose to be Prescott's backup.

Schottenheimer had this to say on the matter Monday, per ESPN's Todd Archer , after the Demercado signing became official (and before Milton was let go).

"We're still piecing the puzzle together, and that's where this thing is very fluid," Schottenheimer said.

The Cowboys ultimately chose Howell as their QB2, making a switch from 2025, when Milton was Prescott's backup. Schottenheimer explained why.

"I think when we looked at the whole body of work, we just felt like Sam had done a little bit more in terms of executing the offense in certain areas," Schottenheimer told reporters on Tuesday, per DallasCowboys.com Staff Writer Tommy Yarrish .

"To have Joe Milton back would be incredible, we'll see what happens with the claims, and then see what he wants to do. We've shown that we know how to develop him. I think him being in this system for another year would be amazing, but I also know that he should have choices. And so, we'll see what happens, but in terms of wanting [Milton] back, absolutely."

Schottenheimer also said it was a "very, very hard decision" en route to choosing Howell, who signed a one-year deal with Dallas this offseason.

Milton did quite well this preseason, completing 29-of-43 passes (67.4 percent) for 378 yards and three touchdowns. Howell impressed as well, going 27-of-40 (67.5 percent) for 314 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

Howell won the battle, but Milton could still be a part of the team's future.

Dallas opens the regular season on Sunday, Sept. 13 at the New York Giants.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Contract Extension Talks Updated By Ravens GM Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson's five-year, $260 million contract expires after the 2027 season, but general manager Eric DeCosta expressed optimism that the team can get an extension done with the two-time NFL MVP by March during a chat with reporters on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson's five-year, $260 million contract expires after the 2027 season, but general manager Eric DeCosta expressed optimism that the team can get an extension done with the two-time NFL MVP by March during a chat with reporters on Wednesday.

Jackson, who is entering his ninth season with the Ravens, is a four-time Pro Bowler and three-time First Team All-Pro who has led Baltimore to the playoffs in six of his campaigns.

Jackson's 8.3 adjusted passing yards per attempt and 102.2 quarterback rating stand first all-time in NFL history, per Pro Football Reference . He's also led the Ravens to a 76-31 record in his starts. Needless to say, it behooves the Ravens to keep the 29-year-old Jackson aboard long-term.

Last year was a tougher campaign for Jackson, who suffered multiple injuries, missed four games and saw his production dip after a 2024 season that ended with him finishing second in the NFL MVP race. Jackson told reporters in August that injuries in particular limited his mobility.

He goes into this season healthy, though, and that represents a chance Jackson can return to his usual form as a game-breaking dual threat.

If so, one can surmise his value would only go up. It's unclear what kind of contract Jackson, who is his own agent, would covet. At the top of the QB market , though, sits Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and his $448 million deal ($64 million average per year).

Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson leads the NFL in total guarantees ($230 million) on his fully guaranteed five-year deal that ends after this season, though one can surmise that's something we may never see for a long time after the contract backfired on the team due to his poor performance.

Otherwise, Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen's $147 million guaranteed leads the way.

Negotiations between Jackson and the Ravens got ugly in March 2023, when Baltimore placed a non-exclusive franchise tag on the quarterback and Jackson requested a trade after saying "the team has not been interested in meeting my value." However, the two sides eventually came together for his current five-year deal, signed in April 2023.

The guess here, based on DeCosta's remarks, is that these negotiations could go smoother than the last time around. In the meantime, the Ravens are getting ready for Week 1 at the Indianapolis Colts on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Disgraced former Ravens kicker Justin Tucker reportedly works out for Jets
articles.summary: Tucker hasn't kicked in an NFL game since his release by the Ravens in 2025 after 16 women accused him of sexual misconduct.
articles.body:
Former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker worked out for the New York Jets on Wednesday, according to multiple reports . Tucker was part of a group workout that also featured Michael Badgley and Josh Karty, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports .

The Jets are in search of a kicker after Jason Sanders missed an extra point and a 54-yard field-goal attempt in Friday's preseason loss to the Giants, concluding a failed competition for the job from training camp. The Jets have since waived Sanders and claimed Blake Grupe off waivers. Sanders is back with the team on the practice squad.

Tucker was an eight-time Pro Bowler and five-time first-team All-Pro for the Baltimore Ravens in 13 seasons with the team. The Ravens released Tucker in 2025 after 16 women accused him of sexual misconduct that he allegedly engaged in repeatedly over the course of years during massage therapy sessions.

Tucker has denied the allegations and was not criminally charged.

Weeks after the Ravens cut Tucker, the NFL announced he was suspended for 10 games for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Tucker has not kicked in an NFL game since.

The Saints and Colts both reportedly worked Tucker out over the summer, but he did not make either roster. With New York's kicker position still unsettled, the Jets are giving Tucker a shot.

Tucker was one of the most accurate and reliable kickers in NFL history during his tenure with the Ravens. But his performance declined in his final season with the team prior to the news of the scandal and his release. He converted a career-low 73.3% of his field-goal attempts in 2024, well below his career conversion rate of 89.1%.

articles.title: Super Bowl-winning coach Charlie ‘Kippy’ Brown, Memphis’ first Black quarterback, dead at 71
articles.summary: Super Bowl-winning coach, the first Black quarterback in Memphis history, Charlie "Kippy" Brown dead at 71 years old. Pete Carroll called him a "great friend."
articles.body: Super Bowl-winning coach Charles "Kippy" Brown died this week at age 71. His cause of death is unknown. Brown began his football career as a quarterback at the University of Memphis from 1974-77, becoming the first Black quarterback in school history. The school inducted Brown into the M Club Hall of Fame in 2016 and he was inducted into the Tennessee Sports Hall of Fame in 2019. He also was honored with the Billy J. Murphy Award. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Sweetwater, Tennessee, native then began his coaching career at his alma mater in 1978. After spending time at Louisville and Tennessee as a wide receivers coach, Brown transitioned to the pro ranks. With the New York Jets he was the team’s running backs coach from 1990-92. He returned to Tennessee for two years to be the team's wide receivers coach after his Jets tenure. Brown then returned to the pro level for the rest of his career, except for one year in 2009 when he went back to Tennessee to be a wide receivers coach. Brown coached for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Miami Dolphins, Green Bay Packers, Houston Texans, Detroit Lions and Seattle Seahawks. He spent one year as the head coach of the Memphis Maniax of the XFL. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! He was the Seahawks' wide receivers coach from 2010-14 when they made consecutive Super Bowl runs. Brown coached Doug Baldwin, Golden Tate, Jermaine Kearse and Sidney Rice and was beloved by his players and fellow staff. "He was a great friend to everybody, because he had such a positive, good, fun-loving spirit," former Seahawks head coach Pete Carroll told the team's website. "Everybody loved being around Kip. And he had a light about him, he wanted to have a good time and have fun and make things pleasant for everyone around him. That's why so many people have rallied around him in this last month or so and reached out to (his wife) Deon, being supportive and loving. He was a wonderful person, and my heart goes out to Deon and the family. It's a beautiful family." Baldwin credited Brown with helping him become the man he is today. "Kippy and Sidney Rice paired really well together as being the elder statesmen in the room, helping us young guys get onboarded into the NFL life. "For me as a young person to have him as my rookie coach, I know I would not have been the player I was if it wasn't for Kippy. I owe a great deal to him as a coach who helped me develop as a player, but also the man that he was, the way that he held us accountable as young men, doing it in a way that was considerate, and we knew he was only doing it because he loved and cared about us, I wouldn't be the man that I am today without Kippy Brown." Brown is survived by his wife, Deon, and his two children, Jennifer and Jeome.

articles.title: Panthers WR Tetairoa McMillan Added 20 Pounds in Offseason, Feels 'Stronger, Faster'
articles.summary: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan added 20 pounds during the offseason while preparing for his second year in the NFL, per Darin Gantt of the team's official website.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan added 20 pounds during the offseason while preparing for his second year in the NFL, per Darin Gantt of the team's official website.

McMillan explained that he wanted to return to his college weight.

"In college when I was heavier, I was stronger, faster," McMillan told reporters Wednesday.

49ers DE's Hilarious Plan for Australia Flight

The 23-year-old previously revealed that he ended last season at 205 pounds, via Kassidy Hill of the team's official website.

In June, McMillan confirmed that he bulked up to roughly 220 pounds.

The former Arizona standout is looking to build on his impressive rookie year, immediately establishing himself as a crucial piece of Carolina's passing attack after he was selected with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft.

McMillan hauled in 70 receptions for 1,014 yards and seven touchdowns while appearing in all 17 regular-season games. He was named Offensive Rookie of the Year for his efforts.

Carolina won the NFC South and advanced to the playoffs, ultimately falling to the Los Angeles Rams in the Wild Card round. Still, McMillan caught five passes for 81 yards in his postseason debut.

The Panthers now enter their 2026 campaign looking to clinch consecutive playoff appearances for the first time since 2015.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty's Injury Status Revealed by Raiders HC Ahead of Week 1 vs. Dolphins
articles.summary: Despite an ankle injury scare during training camp, it seems as if Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty will be available for the team's Sept. 13 opener against the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
Despite an ankle injury scare during training camp, it seems as if Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty will be available for the team's Sept. 13 opener against the Miami Dolphins.

"Yes," Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters Wednesday when asked if he was optimistic Jeanty would play in that contest.

While initial reporting indicated there was significant concern among the running back's teammates when he suffered the injury and was helped off the field, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported last month he avoided a season-ending setback.

"It's nothing like that," Rapoport said. "My understanding... is that it's an ankle sprain believed to be more low than high, and not considered to be a major injury. But it is a real injury, and the reality is, there is a chance that Ashton Jeanty may not be on the field for Week 1. They are hopeful that he will be. There is a chance that he won't be."

Kubiak's comments suggest that Jeanty will be available against the Dolphins, although ESPN's Ryan McFadden reported he didn't practice Wednesday.

Jeanty surely wants to play against a Dolphins team that may be among the Raiders' more favorable opponents of the season.

That would give him an early opportunity to build on his solid but unspectacular play from his rookie season in 2025 when he tallied 975 yards and five touchdowns on the ground behind just 3.7 yards per carry.

Las Vegas made him a franchise building block when it selected him with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2025 NFL draft, and he didn't quite live up to elevated expectations in his first year in the league.

But Jeanty now has a season of experience under his belt and will look to take a second-year leap, assuming he is healthy enough to be on the field when the regular season starts.

articles.title: George Kittle, Nick Bosa make the flight as 49ers head to Australia for historic opener: reports
articles.summary: George Kittle and Nick Bosa made the flight to Australia with the San Francisco 49ers, fueling hopes both stars will suit up against the Rams on Sept. 10.
articles.body: The San Francisco 49ers are on their way to Australia to participate in the first-ever NFL game on the continent against their NFC West foe, the Los Angeles Rams, to kick off the 2026 season. And two specific passengers have fans hopeful heading into next week’s matchup down under. Tight end George Kittle and defensive end Nick Bosa, two very important pieces of Kyle Shanahan’s roster, made the trip with the rest of the team, according to multiple reports. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM This is encouraging considering both have been dealing with their own recovery from injury. Kittle suffered a torn Achilles in the Wild Card Round against the Philadelphia Eagles on Jan. 11, while Bosa tore his ACL in Week 3 last season. Bosa, specifically, has been battling tendinitis for most of the 49ers’ training camp. NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL CONFIRMS LEAGUE WANTS MULTIPLE TEAMS BASED OUTSIDE THE US: 'NO DOUBT' Camp has not been at all pleasant for the 49ers in terms of depth, as multiple players have been dealing with injury, including new wide receiver Mike Evans and fullback Kyle Juszczyk on top of Kittle and Bosa. San Fran also lost wide receiver Ricky Pearsall to a PCL injury. But with Kittle and Bosa heading out to Australia, it could mean that reinforcements are on the way to start the regular season. "I would assume so," Kittle said last month when asked if traveling to Australia would indicate whether or not he’s playing in the game. "I mean, that probably makes the most sense. I would assume." After practicing on Wednesday, the 49ers took flight to Australia, where they’re expected to land on Friday due to the 17-hour time difference. It’s that time difference that the 49ers are making sure players get accustomed to it before they take on the Rams on Sept. 10 at 8:35 p.m. ET. For both teams, it will actually be Friday morning at 10:35 a.m. That’s when kickoff will take place at Melbourne Cricket Ground. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In the days leading up to it, the availability of Kittle, Bosa and the rest of the 49ers should become clear as they hold practices and gear up for a team many believe are Super Bowl favorites this season. The Rams returned MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford, though nobody saw Aaron Donald coming out of retirement to join Myles Garrett on the defensive line after the Defensive Player of the Year was traded for with the Cleveland Browns.

A rookie card featuring New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart has sold for $204,000 on Fanatics Collect, which provided more information.

Dart showed great promise during his 2025 rookie season. Over 12 starts, the former Ole Miss star completed 63.7 percent of his passes for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions. He excelled on the ground, rushing for 487 yards and nine more scores. Dart finished fourth in the Associated Press Offensive Rookie of the Year race.

articles.title: Ravens GM says team is still waiting on NFL investigation of Rashod Bateman's arrest
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta says the team is still waiting on the NFL's investigation into receiver Rashod Bateman's arrest earlier this of...
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. (AP) — Baltimore Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta says the team is still waiting on the NFL's investigation into receiver Rashod Bateman's arrest earlier this offseason.

"In these matters we just really kind of sit back and wait for the league and for the authorities to kind of tell us what's going on," DeCosta said. "Have no indication how long that's going to take."

Bateman was taken into custody in June in Georgia on suspicion of family violence battery and reckless conduct, both misdemeanors, and criminal damage to property, a felony.

"It's obviously something that we're very disappointed about, that we have to deal with these kind of things right now," DeCosta said. "We knew about it right away, we contacted the league right away. Spoke to the league, the league has been doing an investigation."

DeCosta spoke with reporters Wednesday, a normal occurrence shortly before the start of the season. In addition to Bateman's legal issues, he also addressed the team's kicking situation. Baltimore added Jake Moody to the practice squad this week, in effect putting starter Tyler Loop on notice after a shaky preseason.

Loop missed three of his seven field goal attempts in this year's exhibition games.

"We got to make kicks," DeCosta said. "Fresh set of legs to look at, evaluate, compare, see how it all works out. In the end, it's a performance business."

DeCosta also said he remains optimistic about working out a new contract with star quarterback Lamar Jackson. That did not happen this offseason, and the team ended up having to restructure his existing deal, which has two seasons remaining.

The biggest cause for optimism when Baltimore released its 53-man roster last weekend was the fact that defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike was not on injured reserve, which suggests he's expected back at some point in the first four weeks.

Madubuike missed most of last season with a neck injury.

"I'm as encouraged now as I've ever been about Nnamdi," DeCosta said. "Getting him back has been incredible."

articles.title: NFL expert urges 49ers to trade for Maxx Crosby
articles.summary: The 49ers may need to make a big trade to remain competitive in the tough NFC West.
articles.body:
The NFC West is a gauntlet heading into the 2026 NFL season, and the San Francisco 49ers may be falling behind. The Los Angeles Rams beefed up their defense with the additions of Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie before the return of Aaron Donald, and the defending division and Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks still look dominant.

Therefore, NFL Network analyst Brian Baldinger believes the 49ers must make a swing of their own and trade for Las Vegas Raiders star edge rusher Maxx Crosby. Speaking on 95.7 The Game , Baldinger framed the trade as a necessity given what the Rams have already done on the defensive line.

"You're in an arms race with the Rams right now," Baldinger said. "This is like a military arms race trying to keep up. I don't know that Maxx Crosby is available or could be had, I have no idea. All I know is I was at the Sack Summit in Las Vegas a month ago, and nobody could beat him off the line of scrimmage. Everybody challenged him — Jared Verse, pick a guy that was out there — nobody could beat him off the ball. Nobody. He won, and they had an open competition, Maxx — I got it on video — he beat everybody off the ball."

Baldinger also dismissed concerns about the knee issue that scuttled a trade to the Baltimore Ravens back in the spring, drawing on his own playing career for context.

"I know Baltimore basically said that his knee is shot," Baldinger said. "I don't see it. I failed a physical coming in after my sixth year, failed a physical, and played six more years. They said my knee was shot. Everybody evaluates these things differently. But I feel like if you had a chance to get Maxx Crosby, he becomes your best defensive player immediately. It's infectious, the way that he plays the game, the way that he practices. Shanahan's not going to beat him in the building. On any given day, he'll beat everybody in the building. He's got the Michael Jordan mentality."

What would it cost to acquire Crosby? The Ravens traded two first-round picks, but that package seems too pricey now given what unfolded with the deal earlier this year. Bleacher Report's Alex Kay proposed a deal built around a 2027 first-rounder, a 2027 second-rounder and a 2028 third-rounder to pry Crosby loose in the wake of the Rams' Myles Garrett trade.

However, Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer urged caution with any deal, writing that he liked the idea "in principle" but preferred San Francisco wait and see how its aging core performed before selling off draft capital. Crosby himself carries a three-year, $106.5 million extension with $91.5 million guaranteed, signed after the Baltimore deal collapsed.

The 49ers need edge rushing help, though. Nick Bosa is working back from his ACL injury and Mykell Williams is already on the physically unable to perform list and won't play for at least the first four weeks of the season. That leaves a hobbled Bosa, 2026 rookie Romello Height, Sam Okuayinonu and Keion White as the only viable pass rushers on the edge at the moment for San Francisco.

Crosby would be expensive and risky, but likely worth it to remain competitive in the division.
